summary: Remote-controlled agent: WebSocket gateway drives local shell/PTY execution
details: @whalent/agent is a daemon that connects to a WebSocket gateway (defaulting to https://memory.whalent.com) and, per its own README, accepts remote commands (including 'upgrade' and 'restart') from that gateway and auto-starts workers. The shipped bundle imports ws/WebSocket alongside node-pty, @xterm/headless, ssh2, and child_process.spawn, wiring gateway-delivered messages into local shell, PTY, and subprocess execution on the host that runs the agent. Whoever controls the configured gateway can execute arbitrary commands on the installer's machine and trigger a remote self-upgrade of the agent itself. The two shipped bundles (dist/core.cjs ~14 MB and dist/index.cjs) are processed with javascript-obfuscator (hex identifiers, rotated string array, control-flow flattening), so the exact set of commands the gateway can invoke is not auditable from source. The daemon runs only when the operator explicitly launches the `whalent` CLI, but once launched it is a persistent remote-command channel into the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
